questions.title: How can the Ninth Circuit both grant a stay pending appeal and simultaneously order reinstatement of cooperative agreements?
questions.question_body: The panel says it is staying the district court’s preliminary injunctions "in their entirety, except as specified" and then directs the government to reinstate cooperative agreements necessary to provide reception and placement services under 8 U.S.C. § 1522. I'm confused procedurally: isn't reinstating agreements affirmative, injunction-like relief? Under Nken, stays preserve the status quo rather than order new actions. What is the doctrinal basis for issuing affirmative directives within a stay order, and how does the court reconcile that with the traditional limits on stays versus injunctions pending appeal?

questions.title: Does 8 U.S.C. § 1522 impose mandatory duties or merely authorize refugee resettlement services?
questions.question_body: The majority treats § 1522 as imposing statutory obligations to provide reception and placement services, while Judge Lee reads the section as authorizing (not requiring) programs, emphasizing the title and repeated "is authorized" language in §§ 1522(b)-(e). The majority points to § 1522(a)'s "shall" and HHS obligations for unaccompanied minors (§ 1522(d)(2)(B)) and for projects under § 1522(e)(7)(A). What canons of construction and precedent guide whether the "shall" in § 1522(a) converts the authorizations in (b)-(e) into mandates once appropriations exist? Are there cases interpreting § 1522 specifically on mandate vs. authorization?

questions.title: What is the scope of presidential authority under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) to suspend refugee admissions compared to refugee processing and funding decisions?
questions.question_body: Relying on Trump v. Hawaii, the panel suggests the President is likely to prevail on the suspension of refugee entry under § 1182(f). But the funding and service-provision issues seem to be treated separately, potentially under the APA and § 1522. Where is the line between a permissible suspension of "entry" under § 1182(f) and actions that affect domestic resettlement services and contracts post-admission? Are there limits preventing § 1182(f) from being used to indirectly nullify domestic statutory obligations to already-admitted refugees?

questions.title: On what APA grounds is the government "not likely to prevail" regarding defunding and termination of refugee cooperative agreements?
questions.question_body: The order previews that the government is unlikely to win at least one APA challenge tied to § 1522 obligations, but it does not specify the APA theory. Is the issue arbitrary-and-capricious review under § 706(2)(A), contrary-to-law under § 706(2)(A) because it conflicts with § 1522, or failure to follow required procedures (notice-and-comment) if the terminations functioned as a rule/policy change? How do courts generally classify mass termination of cooperative agreements and funding suspensions for APA purposes—final agency action, procurement discretionary action exempt from APA, or programmatic decisions tied to statutory duties?

questions.title: What is the significance of the earlier "limited carveout" for conditionally approved refugees pre–January 20, 2025, and why was it vacated now?
questions.question_body: The motions panel initially denied a stay "to the extent" it applied to individuals conditionally approved before Jan. 20, 2025, then clarified that carveout twice. The present panel vacates those prior stays and issues a new stay with a different carveout focused on § 1522 services for already-admitted refugees. What legal or factual developments justify abandoning the prior conditional-approval carveout? Was the earlier carveout premised on reliance interests or specific statutory rights of conditionally approved applicants, and why does the new order no longer protect that group?

questions.title: Do refugees abroad and resettlement agencies have standing to challenge the entry suspension and funding terminations?
questions.question_body: The plaintiffs include refugees outside the United States approved for resettlement and domestic agencies whose cooperative agreements were terminated. For the noncitizen plaintiffs outside the U.S., what injury and zone-of-interests analyses apply after Trump v. Hawaii and related standing precedents? For the agencies, is loss of cooperative agreements sufficient Article III injury? Is their interest in program administration within the zone of interests of § 1522 or the APA, despite procurement-related discretion and sovereign immunity considerations?

questions.title: How do appropriations constraints interact with alleged statutory mandates in § 1522?
questions.question_body: The order notes FY 2025 appropriations for migration and refugee assistance and an $800 million rescission. Section 1522(a)(1)(A) conditions some obligations "to the extent of available appropriations." If § 1522 imposes duties, how do courts evaluate whether appropriations are "available" and sufficient to compel performance? Can the executive cite reduced appropriations as a basis to terminate all cooperative agreements, or must it scale services consistent with available funds? Are there cases where courts ordered continued services notwithstanding reduced or uncertain appropriations?
